root_cause.text: The delayed work `mlo_scan_start_wk` was not canceled when the virtual interface disconnects (i.e., during station state transition down), allowing it to potentially execute after the vif is freed or during an interface change, leading to use-after-free or init-after-queue vulnerabilities.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(&mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk)` in `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down` (the disconnection path) and removes the cancel from `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif` (vif cleanup). The commit message explicitly states that the work is not canceled on disconnection, causing use-after-free if the work runs after vif is freed, and init-after-queue if it runs after `drv_change_interface`.

intent_record.how: At runtime, during virtual interface (VIF) cleanup, the driver will no longer cancel the pending MLO scan start delayed work. This may prevent potential issues if the cancellation was redundant or could cause a race condition, but it also means the work might still be pending (or already completed) when the VIF structure is freed.

candidates.rationale: The delayed work mlo_scan_start_wk is canceled only during VIF cleanup, but not when the station state transitions down. This leaves a window where the work can execute after the vif is freed or during an interface change, causing use-after-free or init-after-queue. The fix removes this redundant cancellation and adds the necessary cancellation in the station state down path.
